## Functional summary

This 425-amino-acid sequence is most consistent with **RlmN**, a dual-specificity, radical-SAM RNA methyltransferase. The assignment is supported by reviewed RlmN homologs with **45.6–49.7% sequence identity** and broad sequence coverage; the tool grades the evidence as **limited homology support**, so the function is inferred for this particular sequence rather than experimentally confirmed.

RlmN catalyzes **C2 methylation of adenine** in either **A2503 of 23S rRNA** or **A37 of tRNA**, producing 2-methyladenosine (m²A). The curated homolog reactions list two SAM molecules and reduced ferredoxin among the reactants, and 5′-deoxyadenosine, methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), and oxidized ferredoxin among the products. RlmN homologs are annotated to bind a **[4Fe–4S] cluster**; that cofactor assignment is likewise based on homology here.

The 23S rRNA modification is associated with ribosomal proofreading and fidelity.
